Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
An overnight tape, and a healing one. Sean posted no new ticker call — only process (how to run a short book below the moving averages, and a post on traders blaming Wall Street). iain gave the window its two sharpest single-name setups (INTC's inflection test, QCOM's absorption base above the 180s). Enrich ran the busiest board: an Oct 27 watchlist (BE, MRVL, TSLA, RKLB, LMT, XOM, PLTR, NOW), a BE add, a memory call (MU, SNDK, SKHY), and an options edition (see More). Prof ran the bounce list (MU, SNDK, LITE, MRVL, BE, INTC) plus two washed-out names with precise levels (IREN $28, CRWV ~$50) and a KOSPI healing note. Venu added the structural call of the window — IGV building a massive 24-month base with early Stage 2 software candidates — plus the NFLX value-trap question. DiCarlo returned after a quiet window with three calls (APP patience, SKHY breakout, AVGO Smart Money Zone). Remz is the outright bull (a strong trend around the corner after sideways action since June) with next week's midterms as the next event. Your process sides with the watchers over the callers: the genuine qualifier shapes are QCOM's absorption base, the near-highs quiet-volume names (VEEV, TEAM, ZETA), and the at-highs continuations (XOM, GTLB); everything else is a bounce to watch hold, a reclaim that has not fired, a strong day to not chase, or a washout with no bottom yet.

From the group

Sean — process, no new ticker calls: on running a short book — “Regardless if you like to trade the downside or not, every trader should know how to run a short book when the market is trending below its moving averages. A lot of traders think shorting means chasing a stock down after 4 or 5 big red candles… BUT That’s the easiest way to…” — quoted to the visible cutoff — plus a post on traders blaming Wall Street (hedge funds, market makers, algorithms, the Fed) that is also cut off in extraction. His Oct 25 week plan (MU/ASML/LITE/MRVL/DELL shorts, GLD/CBRS/LRCX reversals, SHOP/ZETA/IOT/FROG/RBRK/IBM strength track) was covered in yesterday's feed and is not repeated here; today's posts do not repeat those calls.

iain — process post: the golf analogy — “Imagine trying to play a round of golf with 50 people standing behind you, each telling you which club to use, where to aim, and how hard to swing. Even if you've hit that exact shot a thousand times, eventually you're going to start second-guessing yourself. That's literally…” — quoted to the visible cutoff. His INTC and QCOM calls are rows above.

Enrich — options edition (contracts, not stock setups): “WATCHLIST – OPTIONS EDITION: Leadr’s daily top 5 into tomorrow: 1. $PBR 11/20 $26.50c, 2. $PLTR 11/20 $200c, 3. $MSFT 11/20 $540c, 4. $SNAP 10/30 $6.5c, 5. $SM 11/20 $42.5c. Top contracts are chosen for each based on volume, OI, spreads, greeks, & overall pricing.” PBR, SNAP and SM are not watchlist rows because an options contract is not a stock setup; PLTR and MSFT rows note the contracts where relevant. Also from Enrich: “AI doesn’t trade with emotions” (no ticker), and a reply about robot RAM needs (no trade).

Remz — market feel, no tickers: “Market feels a lot more fluid today” (Oct 26, 11:25 AM ET) plus a link-only post with no text. His trend call is in the SPY panel.

Prof — macro, no new tickers beyond the rows: “KOSPI is pumping hard today. Some healing this week.” plus a process post (“Trading is a game of probabilities” is the IREN post itself, quoted in its row). His bounce list, IREN and CRWV calls are rows above.

Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; posts truncated in the extraction itself (Sean's short-book and blame posts, iain's golf post, Enrich's Oct 27 watchlist tail, Venu's IGV base post, Remz's trend post, Prof's IREN post) are quoted only to the visible cutoff.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Mon Oct 26, 2026 close — this run is pre-market Tuesday, so Monday’s close is the latest completed close and Tuesday’s session is not in any number here. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader’s framing, and it’s labeled every time.
  • Sector lines: each card’s sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Mon Oct 26, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL/LITE/CRWV→XLK, MSFT/PLTR/NOW/WDAY/VEEV/TEAM/GTLB/ADBE/SAP/ASAN/CRM→IGV, NVDA/INTC/QCOM/MRVL/MU/SNDK/SKHY/AVGO→SMH, GOOGL/META/NFLX/ZETA/APP→XLC, AMZN/TSLA/SHOP/CART→XLY, XOM→XLE, RKLB→UFO (space — best fit), TENB→CIBR (cybersecurity — best fit), BE→ICLN (clean energy — best fit), LMT→ITA (aerospace & defense — best fit), IREN→IBIT (spot bitcoin — best fit for a bitcoin miner). Best-fit choices are noted here, not hidden.
  • Where none of the seven commented, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” All four indexes are unavailable this window: no trader posted an index-specific level or call (the SPY panel carries Remz's general-market stance, but it names no index level, so the strip label stays unavailable, as in yesterday’s feed).
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). Flagged qualifier shapes: QCOM (absorption base, trigger above the 180s), VEEV, TEAM and ZETA (tightening near highs on quiet volume), XOM and GTLB (at-highs continuations), SHOP and CRM (above every average with a clear trigger above). Constructive holds, not entries: PLTR, NOW, WDAY, SAP, ASAN. Bounce spots to watch hold, not chase: INTC, BE, MRVL, MU, SNDK, LITE. Reclaim watches, not qualifiers: RKLB ($55), IREN (month-end $28), AVGO (Smart Money Zone), CRWV (washout watch), APP (patience call), NFLX (value-trap question), SKHY (overnight breakout, no trend read). Strong days to not chase: TSLA, LMT, TENB. Explicitly not qualifiers: CART (+7.87% on 8.38x volume — extended), AAPL (holds-only at the highs), MSFT/NVDA/GOOGL/META (chart checks only), AMZN (an add, not a setup).
  • Coverage note: nothing is carried over silently. Yesterday's ideas appear here only where today's posts repeat them (XOM, PLTR, CRM, RKLB, MRVL, MU, LITE, SHOP, ZETA, CART, TSLA, AMZN) — and then only under today's calls, which sometimes differ from yesterday's (MRVL/MU/LITE were Sean's shorts yesterday; today they are Prof's bounce spots and Enrich's watchlist/memory names). Sean's Oct 25 week plan, FROG, IOT, CRWD, OKTA, NTAP, ZS, BP, OXY, GLD, CBRS, LRCX, RBRK, IBM and ISRG are not rows because today's posts do not repeat those calls.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. Stage lives in the pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) and is kept out of the prose and the setup badges; traders’ own quoted words are exempt. SKHY carries a “No 30-wk history” pill instead of a stage: too few weekly closes exist for a 30-week MA or 50-week EMA yet.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. Media URLs exist in the logged-out profile HTML, but they could not be reliably matched to specific posts (the same reason no Prof chart was embedded on Oct 26), so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line’s endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all computable lines passed within 0.5% (most within 0.04%). The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only. SKHY’s 30-week MA and 50-week EMA are not applicable (insufficient history) and are shown as such, not estimated.
